chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad and Abu Dawud together, from Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Al-'Ala', from Ibn Abi Ya'fur, who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who urinated, then performed wudu and stood for the prayer, so he found wetness. He (peace be upon him) said: 'He does not need to perform wudu again; rather, that is from the veins (of urine).
ai.seo_question: Does residual wetness after urination invalidate wudu if one is unsure if it is urine?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) addresses the common doubt of residual wetness (*istibra'*) after urination, ruling that moisture from the urinary veins (*al-haba'il*) does not nullify ablution. This establishes the principle of *al-istishab* (presumption of continuity) in Shia jurisprudence, where the default state of purity is maintained unless certainty of impurity is established, thereby alleviating the burden of *waswas* (doubt) for worshippers.

en.hubeali: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad and Abu Dawood, altogether from Al Husayn Bin Saeed, from Safwan Bin Yahya, from Al A’ala, from Ibn Abu Yafour who said,

‘I asked Abu Abdullahasws about a man who urinates, then he performs Ablution (Wudhu)s and stands for the Prayer, so he finds wetness. Heasws said: ‘He would not perform Ablution (Wudhu). But rather, that is from the sexual veins’.
en.sarwar: 2. A number of our people have narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from and abu Dawud all al-Husayn ibn Sa‘id from Safwan ibn Yahya from al-‘Ala’ ibn abu Ya‘fur who has said the following:

“I once asked abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about a man who urinates, then takes Wudu 5 . He then stands up for Salah (prayer) and finds a certain moisture. He (the Imam) said, ’He does not need Wudu 5 ; it is of Haba’il (passageways, veins).”
